sub_issue: Fees charged for closing account
text:
I had a Certificate of Deposit ( CD ) with Bread Savings ( Comenity Capital Bank ) that recently renewed. I contacted their customer service shortly after the renewal to request early closure and asked for a waiver of the early withdrawal penalty ( {$52.00} ), given my long-standing relationship with them and my intent to close all accounts. They denied my request, citing standard policy. 

There are two key issues Id like to raise in addition to their refusal : Bread Savings uses calendar days ( not business days ) to calculate the CD grace period, which is extremely misleading and unfair to consumers. In my case, the grace period included a weekend and gave me effectively no chance to review the new renewal rate or react without penalty. 

They give customers o

nly 1 calendar day to see the renewal rate before auto-renewing the CD, which is unreasonable. Most banks provide several business days or notify you in advance of the upcoming rate. Bread does not. There was no transparency about the new rate until after renewal, at which point any withdrawal is penalized unless you act immediately. While I understand CDs come with terms, the way Bread Savings structures and enforces these policies feels designed to trap customers rather than serve them. Their practices are rigid and opportunistic, and they place all the burden on the consumer while protecting their own interests at every turn

sub_issue: Problem with fees
text:
I am submitting this complaint regarding undisclosed and disputed charges on my CareCredit account serviced by Synchrony Bank. 

I originally borrowed {$320.00}. I made two payments totaling {$270.00} and reasonably believed my remaining balance was approximately {$51.00}. On XX/XX/2025, I made an additional {$50.00} payment in good faith believing this would close my account. 

Only after making this payment was I informed that my remaining balance consisted primarily of previously undisclosed fees, including Payment Card Security charges, late fees, and paper statement fees.

I was not clearly informed that Payment Card Security was optional, nor did I knowingly enroll or provide affirmative consent for this add-on product. I only learned what this charge was when I contacted customer service, and I was told it was for job loss or emergency coverage. Had this been clearly disclosed at account opening or before charges accrued, I would have declined.

I was also charged for paper statements, which I did not request or authorize. I receive my statements electronically and did not opt into paper billing.

When I contacted customer service to dispute these charges and explained that I am experiencing financial hardship, I was told that fee reversals are limited to once per year and that no further adjustments could be made. I was also told that hardship or insurance-related concerns were not their department, and no escalation or review of my consent was offered.

As a result, despite paying nearly the full original balance, I am being asked to pay an additional {$110.00}, which is largely composed of fees I did not knowingly agree to.

I am requesting a full review of these charges, including whether affirmative consent was obtained for the optional insurance and paper statement fees

text:
I am filing a formal complaint against Discover Bank for failing to adequately address my dispute concerning inaccurate credit reporting on my account. Despite my efforts to resolve this issue amicably through a pre-arbitration settlement offer, Discover Bank and XXXX have not responded with a satisfactory resolution, and I am now seeking assistance from the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ). 

On XX/XX/2024, I sent a pre-arbitration demand letter to Discover Bank. In this letter, I raised several inaccuracies regarding the reporting of my account information, which have caused significant harm to my creditworthiness. These inaccuracies include missing data, conflicting dates, and incomplete account information. In my letter, I offered Discover Bank the opportunity to settle the dispute by paying {$75000.00} to resolve the issue and avoid the need for arbitration or legal action. 

Despite the serious nature of my dispute, Discover Bank failed to respond satisfactorily to my demand for settlement. Instead of addressing the discrepancies or agreeing to a reasonable settlement, their response ignored the details of the inaccuracies and did not make any valid counteroffer. Their failure to address my claims after multiple disputes constitutes a violation of the Fair Credit Reporting Act. 

Specific Violations of the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) : -Violation of 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ) : Discover Bank failed to ensure maximum accuracy in reporting the information on my account, which has led to misleading and incomplete data being reported. 
-Violation of 15 U.S.C . 1681s-2 ( a ) : Discover Bank did not take appropriate action to investigate the inaccuracies in my report and failed to provide the correct information as required by the FCRA. 
-Violation of 15 U.S.C . 1681s-2 ( b ) : After being notified of my dispute, Discover Bank did not conduct a reasonable investigation into the validity of the reported information and failed to update or correct the data accordingly. 
-Violation of 15 U.S.C . 1681c ( a ) ( 5 ) & 15 U.S.C. 1681c ( i ) : The incomplete and inconsistent information regarding payment history, charge-off dates, and account balances has led to my credit report being inaccurately reported, which violates the FCRA.

On XX/XX/year>, the Chase mobile app displayed the message Youre already approved for a credit card. Based on this representation, I submitted an application under the belief that approval was guaranteed. 

On the same day ( XX/XX/scrub>XXXX XXXX XXXX, Chase denied the application but still placed a hard inquiry on my credit file. This resulted in an immediate and negative impact to my credit score.

On XX/XX/year>, Chase called me directly. During this call, I was again re-denied, even after I repeated my explanation that the application was induced by the misleading already approved message.

The misleading message remained visible for days after denial, compounding the confusion. 
I believe this conduct constitutes a deceptive practice under the CFPBs UDAAP standards ( Unfair, Deceptive, or Abusive Acts or Practices ). Chase induced me to apply under a false sense of certainty, then harmed my credit profile when the representation proved untrue. 

I am requesting that the CFPB review Chases practices and require corrective action, including : Removal or reclassification of the hard inquiry to a soft inquiry, or Approval of a credit line consistent with the already approved representation.

text:
I am filing a complaint against Calvary Portfolio Services and XXXX regarding violations of the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ) in connection with attempts to collect on a debt governed by an arbitration clause. The original contract, which was originated by XXXX, includes an arbitration clause that requires any disputes related to the debt to be resolved through arbitration, not through traditional debt collection methods. Despite this, Calvary Portfolio Services, acting on behalf of XXXX, has continued to pursue collection efforts without adhering to the terms of the arbitration agreement. 
In addition to failing to respect the arbitration clause, also violated the FDCPA by failing to properly verify the debt in accordance with 15 USC 1692g. The FDCPA mandates that debt collectors provide adequate verification of the debt within five days of their initial communication. Calvary Portfolio Services has not provided proper verification or the necessary documentation to comply with the debt validation requirements outlined in the FDCPA. 
As such, Calvary Portfolio Services has violated my consumer rights by continuing collection efforts despite the debt being subject to arbitration, and by failing to verify the debt as required under 15 USC 1692g. These actions mirror violations identified in previous case law. For example, in XXXX v. XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX ( No. XXXX, XXXX Cir. XXXX ), the court ruled that Calvary Portfolio Services violated the FDCPA by continuing collection efforts without providing proper debt verification. Similarly, in XXXX v. XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX ( No. XXXX, XXXX Cir. XXXX ), the court found that Calvary Portfolio Services failed to provide the proper documentation necessary for debt verification under the FDCPA. 
I request that the CFPB investigate this matter and ensure that XXXX and Calvary Portfolio Services cease all collection efforts and adhere to the arbitration clause outlined in the original contract that was originated by XXXX. I further request that Calvary Portfolio Services be held accountable for their violations of consumer protection laws under the FDCPA, and that XXXX be investigated for their failure to ensure compliance with the arbitration provision in their agreement. Delete this collection from my credit report immediately.

text:
I am filing this complaint because the company failed to properly validate a debt I disputed. Under the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), 15 U.S.C. 1692g ( b ), and related consumer protection statutes, a consumer has the right to request a full and verifiable validation of any alleged debt before it can be collected or reported.

I exercised this right and formally requested specific documentation to prove the validity and ownership of the alleged account. The company responded by sending only a generic bank statement. This does not meet the legal standard for debt validation, as it fails to prove the existence, ownership, and enforceability of the alleged debt. 

Specifically, the company failed to provide the following documents I demanded, which are necessary to establish legal standing and verification : Original signed contract Proof that I personally entered into a binding agreement with the original creditor. 

Full chain of title All assignments, transfers, and ownership records from the original creditor to the present entity. 

Proof of Holder in Due Course status As required under the Uniform Commercial Code ( UCC ) Articles 3 and 9.

Transfer documents under 15 U.S.C. 1641 ( g ) ( TILA ) Showing legal transfer and notice of such transfer.

Pooling and Servicing Agreement identification If the alleged debt was securitized, the PSA and Schedule of Assets identifying the specific account. 

By failing to provide these documents, the company has not validated the alleged debt. A mere bank statement does not prove liability, ownership, or the legal right to collect. Therefore, the continued reporting or collection activity on this account constitutes a violation of my rights under the FDCPA and the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( b ).

text:
I am filing a formal complaint regarding Zelle 's failure to investigate unauthorized transactions and its inadequate dispute resolution process. My financial institution, in collaboration with Zelle, has failed to comply with federal consumer protection laws by refusing to properly investigate my claims and denying my ability to recover lost funds. 

1. Failure to Investigate Unauthorized Transactions : Under the Electronic Fund Transfer Act ( EFTA ) ( 15 U.S.C. 1693f ) and Regulation E ( 12 C.F.R. 1005.11 ), financial institutions are required to investigate errors related to electronic fund transfers, including unauthorized transactions. However, my financial institution and Zelle dismissed my dispute without conducting a proper investigation, in direct violation of these regulations. 

2. Unfair and Deceptive Practices : The Consumer Financial Protection Act ( CFPA ) ( 12 U.S.C. 5531 ( a ) ) prohibits unfair, deceptive, or abusive acts or practices ( UDAAP ). Zelle 's refusal to track disputed transactions, failure to provide adequate recourse, and misleading claims that recovering funds is " impossible '' constitute unfair and deceptive practices that leave consumers unprotected.

3. Systemic Issues Identified by the CFPB : The CFPB 's recent lawsuit against Zelle highlights systemic issues, including the platform 's failure to implement effective fraud prevention measures and its repeated allowance of bad actors to exploit the system. Zelle 's lack of accountability places consumers at heightened risk of financial harm.

text:
Subject : Request for Investigation Potential ILSA Violation by NVR , Inc. ( XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX Dear CFPB Enforcement Division, I respectfully request that the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau investigate NVR , Inc. for potential violations of the Interstate Land Sales Full Disclosure Act ( ILSA ) in connection with its marketing and sale of homes in a large-scale waterfront community known as XXXX XXXX in Rehoboth Beach , Delaware. 

Allegation Summary NVR , Inc. is building a 217-lot residential community at XXXX XXXX XXXX To date, it has sold over 140 homes. As part of its sales effort, NVR heavily marketed amenities including a bay beach, marina, kayak launch, and kayak storage shelter. 

However : These amenities were not approved by the appropriate authorities ( e.g., XXXX XXXX, XXXX ) at the time of marketing and sale ; In some cases, such as the " bay beach, '' the features were legally or physically impossible to build due to zoning, environmental restrictions, or regulatory barriers ; NVR failed to disclose the uncertain or speculative status of these amenities during the sales and closing process ; And many homeowners purchased based on renderings and representations that created the impression of guaranteed, imminent delivery. 

This is a textbook case of deceptive inducement under ILSA, where unapproved amenities in a multi-lot development were used to influence buyers without legally required disclosures. NVR has since filed a lawsuit against the developer, admitting that these amenities remain unbuilt and acknowledging the growing frustration of residents. Nevertheless, NVR continued selling homes at premium prices based on these amenity promises.

Request I urge the CFPB to open an investigation into NVRs compliance with ILSA and real estate disclosure obligations, specifically : Whether NVR filed a proper Property Report under ILSA, Whether it disclosed the true regulatory status of the amenities at the time of sale, And whether its conduct constitutes material misrepresentation or fraudulent inducement in violation of federal law.

I am willing to provide marketing materials, legal filings, and supporting testimony from affected homeowners.

sub_issue: Delays with the closing process
text:
We applied for and were approved for what would be our third home loan with Rocket Mortgage. One week prior to our scheduled closing date, Rocket pulled our credit. They said that it was not usually done so close to closing but they had detected a name discrepancy in my husbands history. This was never fully explained but only alluded to. As the credit was one point less than the negotiated terms for the loan they asked us to work with their credit team to raise the score one point. As this delay necessitated delaying the closing, the seller requested information regarding the delay. Rocket then communicated specific credit information to the seller and his agent. When we asked about this, several loan officers said they did not know the sellers representative was not a dual agent. As they had the purchase and sales agreement from the time of the mortgage application this was an egregious error.

The delayed closing, along with the indiscretion of the revelations to the seller caused hardships for all parties.

In addition to this violation, in our view Rocket stumbled numerous times throughout the mortgage approval process. We were assigned an inexperienced agent who called us multiple times a day, seven days a week, but did not seem to be able to process the information we gave him efficiently. We were finally transferred to a supervisor, seven days before closing. However, the supervisor was then the responsible party for revealing the credit information.

We were very frustrated with the entire process and we would not recommend Rocket again. In the past 10 years or so as mortgage companies have streamlined the application and servicing, we have found Rocket to be easy to work with. However, as their fees are not necessarily competitive, I would now not recommend them. We had a miserable experience and received no compensation for the frustration. 

Update : Homeowners insurance paid through monthly payments to Rocket.

Insurance company sent a cancellation notice to us this week because Rocket underpaid the insurance premium for which they received a hill.

text:
Company : InComm / Vanilla Visa Product : Prepaid Gift Card ( Vanilla Visa ) I am filing a complaint regarding an unauthorized fraudulent transaction on a Vanilla Visa prepaid gift card.

The card was purchased legally and stored unused in a secure location ( a home safe ). It was not lost, shared, or used by me or anyone in my household. When I later checked the balance, I discovered an unauthorized charge of {$490.00} that occurred approximately 18 months prior, without my knowledge or consent. 

This fraudulent transaction was discovered only when I checked the balance, as prepaid gift cards do not provide statements or alerts. 

Once the unauthorized charge was discovered, I immediately : Contacted Vanilla Visa customer service Filed a fraud dispute Provided all requested information Vanilla Visa denied the dispute solely due to the transaction being outside the card networks dispute timeframe, not because the charge was determined to be legitimate. 

This was a case of unauthorized fraud, not a delayed reporting issue caused by negligence. The card was unused and secured, and there was no reasonable way to detect the theft earlier. 

The denial appears to be based entirely on internal time limits rather than an evaluation of : Whether the transaction was authorized Whether the merchant was associated with known fraud Whether goodwill or discretionary reimbursement was possible Given the lack of consumer protections for prepaid cards and the absence of balance alerts or statements, this creates an unfair outcome for consumers acting in good faith. 

I am requesting : A secondary review or escalation of this fraud case Consideration of a goodwill reimbursement Transparency regarding the merchant that processed the fraudulent transaction I am not disputing that time limits exist, but I am requesting a fair review based on the facts of unauthorized use and the reasonable inability to detect the fraud earlier.

Specifically, it prohibits the disclosure of personally identifiable information from a student 's education records without the student 's written consent, except in certain circumstances. A violation of this law occurs if a student 's records are improperly shared or made accessible to unauthorized individuals, which has happened in my case.

I am the victim of identity theft, and this account was fraudulently opened in my name without my knowledge or consent. 

To support my claim, I have submitted : A Federal Trade Commission ( FTC ) Identity Theft Report A police report filed with the local authorities documenting this crime Written disputes sent to Santander Consumer USA and XXXX under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), 15 U.S.C. 1681c-2, which provides for blocking of information resulting from identity theft Despite my efforts, the account remains on my credit report, seriously damaging my credit score and history. Under FCRA Section 605B, once a consumer provides proper documentation of identity theft ( FTC affidavit and police report ), the credit reporting agencies are required to block the fraudulent information from appearing on the consumer 's credit report within 4 business days.

Additionally, Santander Consumer USAs continued reporting of this fraudulent account after notification may violate 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( a ), which prohibits furnishers from providing inaccurate information to credit reporting agencies.

sub_issue: Loan balance remaining after the vehicle is repossessed and sold
text:
I am filing this complaint against Ally Financial for multiple violations of the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) and Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ) related to inaccurate and unlawful credit reporting practices. 
SUMMARY OF VIOLATIONS : Ally Financial has furnished grossly inaccurate information to the credit bureaus regarding my repossessed vehicle ( XXXX ), causing severe damage to my credit profile. 
1. FAILURE TO APPLY AUCTION SALE PROCEEDS After my vehicle was repossessed and sold at auction, Ally FAILED to apply the sale proceeds to my outstanding loan balance. The balance being reported does not reflect the auction sale amount, resulting in an artificially inflated debt. This violates FCRA 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ), which requires furnishers to provide accurate and complete information.

2. DOUBLE COUNTING - REPORTING BOTH REPO AND CHARGE-OFF My credit reports show this account being reported as BOTH a repossession AND a charge-off. This is the same debt being counted twice, which : Artificially inflates my total debt obligations Damages my credit score multiple times for a single account Violates FCRA 's accuracy requirements under 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( a ) ( 1 ) A single account can not be reported as both a repossession and a charge-off. This is double counting and is prohibited.

3. INCONSISTENT REPORTING ACROSS BUREAUS The amount reported to Equifax differs from the charge-off amount reported to the other credit bureaus.

This irregular reporting pattern demonstrates Ally 's failure to maintain accurate records and furnish consistent information as required by FCRA. 
4. INACCURATE PAYMENT HISTORY The payment history being reported contains false and inaccurate information that does not reflect my actual payment performance on this account.

5. FAILURE TO PROVIDE REQUIRED NOTICES - FDCPA VIOLATION Ally failed to provide proper notices to both parties as required under the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act 15 U.S.C. 1692e. This constitutes deceptive practices in connection with debt collection.

6. FAILURE TO INVESTIGATE DISPUTES - FCRA 611 ( a ) and 623 ( b ) I have disputed these inaccuracies with the credit bureaus on multiple occasions. Despite receiving notice of my disputes, Ally has : Failed to conduct a reasonable investigation Failed to review all relevant information Failed to correct the inaccurate information Continued to verify false information This violates FCRA 15 U.S.C. 1681i ( a ) and 1681s-2 ( b ).

My signed retail installment contract clearly states that my monthly payment is {$630.00} for 72 months. I have never missed or been late on a payment. 

Recently, I was notified that my monthly payment had been increased from {$630.00} to {$670.00}, and at another time was told the amount should be {$650.00}. None of these amounts match the contract that I agreed to and signed. No valid documentation, contract modification, or written explanation has been provided to justify these changes. 

This attempted increase is unauthorized, inaccurate, and a direct violation of the terms outlined in my binding finance contract. Furthermore, the vehicles original price was approximately {$36000.00}, yet I was financed for around {$50000.00}. Now that the vehicle is almost paid off, the sudden increase in monthly payments raises serious concerns regarding the accuracy of my account and how my payments have been applied. 

I am requesting the following in writing : XXXX reinstatement of my original monthly payment of {$630.00}, as stated in my signed contract. A complete and itemized account history, including all payment applications, principal, interest, and any fees. A written explanation for the attempted increase and any personnel notes or system entries related to this change. Correction of any errors in my account balance or payment schedule.

This letter serves as a formal dispute under the Fair Credit Billing Act ( FCBA ) and all applicable state consumer protection laws. I expect a written response within the legally required timeframe. 

Until this matter is fully resolved in writing, the original contracted payment of {$630.00} must remain in effect. 

Thank you for your prompt attention and cooperation. I look forward to your written resolution. 

Sincerely, XXXX XXXX XXXX

text:
CFPB COMPLAINT NARRATIVE : I enrolled in Honda Financial Services ' XXXX  automatic payment system, scheduled to withdraw payments three days before each due date. In XXXX and XX/XX/year>, Honda 's system misapplied my automatic payments ( arbitrarily as told to me by an XXXX person on the phone ) to sales tax instead of my monthly lease obligation, causing those months to be reported as delinquent. 
I was not effectively notified of this error. Honda left a voicemail on a landline I don't monitor ( XXXX ) rather than my primary cell phone, and I did not immediately open mailed statements since my payments were automatic. 
When I discovered the issue in XX/XX/year> by my bank, I immediately contacted XXXX and a representative confirmed the system had misapplied my payments to sales tax. I paid the outstanding balance ( approximately {$1500.00} ) over the phone immediately to bring the account current. 
On XX/XX/year>, I sent Honda a formal goodwill letter explaining that this delinquency resulted from THEIR system error, not my failure to pay. I requested removal of the negative credit reporting as appropriate given that their system caused the problem. 
Honda responded on Monday XX/XX/XXXX stating only that " the information is accurate '' and they have " an obligation to report correctly. '' This response is inadequate. While it is technically true that payments were late, Honda 's response ignores the fact that the delinquency was caused entirely by THEIR automated system misapplying my scheduled payments. I fulfilled my obligation by enrolling in automatic payments ; Honda 's system failed to process them correctly. 
The negative reporting has caused my credit score to drop from the XXXX to barely XXXX. This does not accurately reflect my creditworthiness or payment history. 
I am requesting that Honda Financial Services remove the negative credit reporting for XXXX and XX/XX/year> from all three credit bureaus.

sub_issue: Billing problem
text:
I am experiencing predatory lending and servicing issues with Credit Acceptance Corporation regarding my auto loan for a XXXX XXXX XXXX. I entered into the contract in XX/XX/XXXX with an APR of 25.99 % and a monthly payment of {$370.00}. 

Despite making numerous payments, my past-due balance frequently did not decrease and in some cases increased, even when I made multiple payments in a single month. The way Credit Acceptance applies payments appears designed to prioritize interest and fees over reducing my principal or bringing the account current. 

Around XX/XX/XXXX, I suffered a job loss, which caused financial hardship. During this period, Credit Acceptance continued to add late fees almost every month and charged daily interest at 25.99 %, which made it nearly impossible to catch up. Partial payments were accepted but did not meaningfully reduce the past-due amount, causing a cycle of permanent delinquency. 

In XXXX, my vehicle was repossessed. I paid approximately {$700.00} to Credit Acceptance to recover the vehicle, plus additional fees to the towing company. My account history shows a repossession cost of {$300.00} being charged, then reversed, then re-applied, which raises concerns about the accuracy and transparency of their accounting. Past-due amounts often remained the same even after payments were made Late fees were repeatedly added Interest charges are extremely high and consume most of my payments Repossession-related fees and reversals are confusing and inconsistent I believe Credit Acceptances servicing practices are unfair, abusive, and deceptive. Their structure traps borrowers in delinquency and makes it extremely difficult to ever become current or significantly reduce the principal. I am asking the CFPB to review my account for improper fee assessments, misapplication of payments, and unfair or abusive practices.
